reader.requirement: At --std 85, every reference in a called program to a USING operand (and its subordinates and redefiners) is resolved by the called program's own Linkage Section description - category, scale, sign, editing, subordinate layout and OCCURS DEPENDING ON - over the argument's storage (BY REFERENCE) or a copy of it (BY CONTENT), whatever description the caller gave the argument.
reader.edition-search: grep -n 'Edition|CobolVersion|Dialect' over ProgramEmitter.cs (only line 101, the module registrar record stamping comp.Edition), CodeGen/Verbs/CallEmitter.cs (only ExternalizedNameInEdition, the program-name spelling of GR1, not formal resolution) and Runtime/Control/CallAbi.cs (none). The formal adoption is one edition-free switch over CallCrossing; the formal carrier is typed from the callee's own DataItem.

reader.notes: The formal's carrier is built from the callee's Linkage description and adopted over the argument's image, so numeric, edited, group and ODO formals all read the caller's storage through their own description. The probe's BY CONTENT pair is of different descriptions, which GR1 forbids the user, so only its BY REFERENCE halves and the caller-side invariance are evidence.

All resolve through the callee's description. cite.py: OK §1985:X.5.1 GR3 the text is in GR3; OK §1985:X.5.1 GR4c. SIDE FINDING (not GR3, the X.5.1 general format; under-rejects): 'PROCEDURE DIVISION USING BY REFERENCE LX.' and 'PROCEDURE DIVISION USING REFERENCE LX.' compile at --std 85 with exit 0 and no diagnostic (r2by-001, r2byr-001), though the 1985 header format is 'PROCEDURE DIVISION [ USING { data-name-1 } … ]' (cite.py: OK §1985:X.5.1 the text is in the clause; same in VI at line 5494). BY VALUE (COBOL0900 pd-header-by-value-2002) and RETURNING (COBOL0900) are refused. No kb/Work note found (grep 'DIVISION USING BY' over kb/Work: only 2002+ method notes).
